messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT 1971000000 — High 5xx spike detected on smart-routing tiering in eu-west. Triggered at 1971000000. Paging oncall.

alice: I'm oncall and watching dashboards now. 5xx ~12% in eu-west-prod between 09:12–09:16 UTC. Root responses are L7 502/503s.

sam: correlating metrics — queue latency up, KV cache miss rate climbing on dedicated pools. Looks aligned with a routing weight change. @maya any recent routing edits?

maya: no runtime deploys in last 2h. We did push a smart-routing policy tweak yesterday that passed canary. Pulling router decision logs to investigate.

maya: log excerpt:
```
[09:13:02] route_decision: user_tier=standard -> prefer=eu-west-latency (weights: latency=0.8,cost=0.2)
[09:13:03] backend: gpu-a1 overloaded -> fallback to gpu-a2
[09:13:04] backend: gpu-a2 rate_limited -> 502
```

priya: support is getting pings — customers see timeouts and some 502s. Hypothesis: aggressive latency weighting routed too much traffic to low-latency pool and exhausted it.

alice: propose immediate mitigations: 1) lower latency weight in eu-west smart-routing to 0.5; 2) apply short-term per-customer rate cap on standard tier; 3) enable regional-steer to spillover to eu-central if eu-west pool >85% utilization.

ben: applying routing weight change now.
```
# rbctl routing update --region eu-west --policy smart-routing --set "latency_weight=0.5"
```
ben: change applied at 1971000065. Change id rp-1971000065.

ops-bot: deploybot: routing policy smart-routing (eu-west) updated by ben. Change id rp-1971000065. CI checks: OK.

alice: setting temporary quota: standard tier -> 120 rps per customer in eu-west to reduce head-of-line effects.
```
# rbctl quota set --tier standard --region eu-west --rate 120
```
ben: quota set applied at 1971000102.

zoe: updating status page: posting "degraded" — customers may see transient 5xx or elevated latency in EU for ~10–30m while we rebalance. Link will be shared.

sam: metrics: immediate drop in 5xx to ~3.5% after weight + quota changes. GPU-a1 CPU trending down. KV miss still elevated but trending toward normal.

maya: enabling regional steer from eu-west -> eu-central for standard tier with threshold 0.85 to offload when capacity high. Cross-region will slightly increase p95 but should stop the cascade.
```
# rbctl steer enable --from eu-west --to eu-central --tier standard --threshold 0.85
```
maya: steer enabled at 1971000150.

alice: support please confirm status page updated to "degraded" and include mitigations and ETA. @zoe

zoe: done — status: degraded — message posted 09:18 UTC. https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1971000000

priya: customer impact summary: approx 6 enterprise tenants experienced >10% error rates; mobile SDK traffic more affected due to sticky routing. Flagged top 3 for outreach.

ben: suggest holding quota at 120 for 1h, then reassess. Thoughts?

alice: agree. Schedule an automatic rollback in 1h if no regressions and add to runbook.

alice: postmortem notes (early): probable root cause — aggressive latency weighting in smart-routing exposed a capacity cliff in the eu-west low-latency pool causing cascaded fallback and head-of-line saturation. Immediate mitigations worked. Longer-term: dynamic thresholding, slower policy ramps, per-backend queue observability.

sam: creating follow-ups: 1) add per-backend queue depth alarms, 2) refine auto-steer thresholds and cooldowns, 3) formal playbook for oncall weight vs quota adjustments. Assigning to eng-runtime + infra.

maya: I'll own 2 & 3. Plan: add canary checks that include pool saturation signals before increasing latency weight, and a simulated spill test during canary.

zoe: outreach sent to top customers; no legal/contract escalations.

ben: current metrics: 5xx at 0.9%, latency stable. Monitoring for 30m.

inc-bot: INCIDENT 1971000000 — mitigations applied. Status: mitigated -> monitoring. last_update 1971000280.

alice: closing active page. Handoff note: if eu-west 5xx >3% again, revert latency_weight to 0.3 and raise quota to 150 temporarily. @ben taking next watch window.

ben: taking watch. Signing off from active page."
